title: TransportClose
description: Why the server ended a client connection. One closed vocabulary spans both sides of the WebSocket upgrade: after the upgrade it is carried in the close frame's reason slot and in the departure control frame; before the upgrade — where no close frame exists — it is carried in the JSON rejection body's code field.

closeReason.title: TransportCloseReason
closeReason.description: The closed vocabulary. A client-side sentinel for a departure that carried nothing is deliberately absent: by construction nothing arrives, so it cannot be a server value, and making it one would invite a server to send it. A departure carrying no reason is an unattributed loss the client classifies locally and never dresses as one of these.

departureControlFrame.title: DepartureControlFrame
departureControlFrame.description: The application-level half of the two-step close adr-20260624-0011 established: sent whenever the connection is still writable, immediately before the close frame, carrying the same reason. This is the first published shape of the {"k":"c"} frame; before it, the June ADR recorded the cause as a string in `code` while the implementation put it in `data` and left `code` an always-omitted int, and nothing could catch the divergence.

data.description: Pre-taxonomy free-form payload, retained verbatim so shipped clients that match literals against it keep working. Not a vocabulary: new readers use `reason`.

code.description: Legacy numeric slot. Always absent in production — every call site passes 0 and the encoder omits it. Retained only because the encoder can still emit it.

sessionId.description: Routing for server-initiated surface severance. Absent on connection-level departures.

preUpgradeRejection.title: PreUpgradeRejection
preUpgradeRejection.description: A rejection that happens before websocket.Accept cannot carry a close reason, so it carries the same vocabulary in its body. This is what makes a rejected credential distinguishable from a dropped connection, which are both a failed handshake to a client that has nothing to read.
